name: Morse.index
difference: Infinite-dimension encoding: the project's index is Mathlib's sigNeg, bounded by finrank ℝ E, hence 0 for every infinite-dimensional E; the blind sSup over finite-dimensional negative-definite subspaces is the true (finite) index when that is bounded. On ℓ²(ℕ), H(x, y) = -(x₀y₀) has project index 0 and blind index 1.
why: In finite dimension, the project's Morse.index_isGreatest plus csSup gives equality. The infinite-dimensional difference is a convention, documented for sigNeg, and lies outside §2; the project uses a separate ℕ∞-valued formIndex for the infinite-dimensional path-space Hessians of Part III, so Morse.index is never applied there.
